item.title: ¿ICE estará en el Super Bowl? Lo que se sabe hasta ahora
item.description: Faltan pocos días para que el Super Bowl llegue al Área de la Bahía y sigue la incertidumbre sobre el posible papel de ICE en la seguridad del evento. Hemos cuestionado a funcionarios locales y federales para saber más.

item.title: The Super Bowl Party Is Here. Fans Are Excited, Even if It’s Seahawks vs Patriots
item.description: A kickoff event on Monday in downtown San José marks the start of the Bay Area’s weeklong celebrations ahead of Super Bowl LX at Levi’s Stadium.

item.title: Super Bowl LX Tickets: Don’t Fall for an (Expensive) Scam
item.description: With the Big Game in Santa Clara only a few days away, scammers are offering fake tickets for thousands of dollars. Know how to not fall for these traps.

item.title: Fire Causes Major Damage to SF’s Mel’s Drive-In on Lombard Street
item.description: An early morning fire broke out in the iconic San Francisco diner’s attic area, near its kitchen hood, according to the Fire Department.

item.title: Big Bear Ski Resorts, Businesses Face Challenging Winter
item.description: Rain and unusually warm temperatures have dominated and put a chill on ski resorts and businesses in the region.

item.title: Some California High-Speed Rail Records Could Remain Secret Under Proposed Law
item.description: California created an inspector general to monitor its long-delayed high-speed rail project. Now, one lawmaker wants to allow that office to withhold some investigative records from the public.

item.title: 2 Teens Arrested in Fatal Triple Shooting Near San Francisco Playground
item.description: The tragic death of a 15-year-old girl marks the city’s second homicide this year.

item.title: San Francisco Teachers Strike: What Should Families Know?
item.description: San Francisco teachers are gearing up for a strike this month, possibly halting most education operations in the city’s schools. From closures to child care, here’s what we know.

item.title: As California Cities Grow Wary of Flock Safety Cameras, Mountain View Shuts Its Off
item.description: After finding that federal agencies accessed its automated license plate reader data, the Mountain View Police Department said this week that it has turned the cameras off.

item.title: Trump and Newsom Find Rare Common Ground on Banning Wall Street Investments in Single-Family Homes
item.description: Critics argue banning institutional investors from buying single-family homes would do little to improve housing affordability today, pointing to alternative solutions like boosting new construction.
